sents.en: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster.
sents.ko: 평소 인색한 친구가 관대함을 북돋우는 약을 먹은 뒤 기꺼이 너에게 크리스마스 선물을 사 준다고 상상해 보라.

sents.en: Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action.
sents.ko: 분명히 그 행동에는 칭찬받을 만한 데가 있다.

sents.en: You’d be pleased to receive the gift.
sents.ko: 너는 그 선물을 받아서 기쁠 것이다.

sents.en: You’d say ‘thank you’, and mean it.
sents.ko: 너는 ‘고마워’라고 말할 것이고, 그 말은 진심일 것이다.

sents.en: But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying.
sents.ko: 하지만 그의 마음의 변화가 온전히 만족스럽지는 않다.

sents.en: According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous.
sents.ko: 미국의 철학자 Zagzebski의 견해로는, 그는 참으로 관대한 사람이 아니다.

sents.en: When we praise someone’s character, we use words for various virtues: ‘generous’, ‘kind’, ‘courageous’, etc.
sents.ko: 우리는 누군가의 성품을 칭찬할 때 ‘관대한’, ‘친절한’, ‘용감한’ 등 여러 미덕을 나타내는 말을 쓴다.

sents.en: A person who gives one gift isn’t generous.
sents.ko: 선물을 한 번 주는 사람이 관대한 것은 아니다.

sents.en: Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person’s ‘moral identity’, an emotional habit that is part of who you are.
sents.ko: 오히려 관대함은 한 사람의 ‘도덕적 정체성’에서 안정된 부분, 곧 네가 어떤 사람인지를 이루는 감정의 습관이다.

sents.en: Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history.
sents.ko: 그러므로 미덕은 평소답지 않은 충동과 달리 네가 살아온 내력의 결과이다.

sents.en: They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed.
sents.ko: 미덕은 네 성품이 어떻게 형성되었는지의 일부이므로 네가 어떤 사람인지의 일부이다.
따라서 즉석에서 얻는 미덕은 있을 수 없다.

sents.en: Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.
sents.ko: 알약 하나를 삼키는 것이 너를 더 좋은 사람으로 만들어 줄 수는 없다.

runs.t: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster.
How would you feel?
Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action.
You’d be pleased to receive the gift.
You’d say ‘thank you’, and mean it.
But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying.
According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous.
When we praise someone’s character, we use words for various virtues: ‘generous’, ‘kind’, ‘courageous’, etc.
A person who gives one gift isn’t generous.
Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person’s ‘moral identity’, an emotional habit that is part of who you are.
Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history.
They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed.
Instant virtue is therefore impossible.
Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.

runs.t: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster.

According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous.
